newsitem.title: BRAZIL: LatAm shrs seen firm this week, but Brazil weakens.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shrs seen firm this week, but Brazil weakens.

text.p: Equities in most Latin American bolsas are seen firming this week on foreign buying and domestic factors, except for Brazil where investors remain concerned over CVRD's privatization, analysts said.

Brazilian shares are seen mixed to lower amid worries over the much-awaited auction of the world's largest iron ore producer, which has been delayed due to a host of legal challenges, local brokers said.

Analysts are unsure whether the government will be able to move ahead the sale this week. The auction, originally slated for April 29, hinges on a high court judge mulling a government appeal against all injunctions blocking the sell-off, who said he may take a decision Tuesday.
"The auction will happen but we are not sure when," a senior trader said. "Everything is in the hands of the judiciary."
Slow progress in the government's civil service reform, seen as key to Brazil's plans to cut public spending, is another factor weighing on the Brazilian bolsa, brokers said.
Congressional officials expect to finish voting on amendments to the administrative reform this week, but traders are skeptical that the voting will take place.
Despite the impasse over the CVRD sale, the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) rose 3.5 percent to end at 10,074 points last week.

In Venezuela, stocks are seen firming on renewed foreign confidence after the country extended its stand-by program with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for another 18 months and April inflation data released Friday fell within market forecasts.

"(April) inflation figures were in line with market expectations, there have been favorable comments from the IMF recently ... and the approved increase in the minimum wage shouldn't be too inflationary," said Banesco broker Simon Brad.
Last week, the bolsa's 19-share index gained 0.7 percent to 6,365.45 points.
Argentine shares were seen continuing their recovery this week in rising turnover as the corporate results period unfolds, dealers said.
"The market is slowly resuming its upward path, helped by the good results of leading companies," said Emilio Alessandro, of Brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip Merval index rose 2.4 percent last week to 732.3 points, cheered by rallies on New York markets and profits of local YPF and Telefonica.
In Mexico, stocks could notch up gains on bargain-hunting and buying by international investors after several sessions in the doldrums, analysts said.
The IPC share index ended Friday at 3,764.88 points, up 0.22 percent.
Chilean equities were expected to hold steady this week but could see modest increases as speculation grows that the Central Bank may cut interest rates, brokers said.

"Interest rates will have to come down again, half a point or so. When that happens, I think we can say the adjustment period is over," said economist Hernan Bravo at Consultants Julion Sales, who said a rate cut was possible in mid-June.
The blue-chip index ended Friday at 119.34 points,. up 1.9 percent, for the whole four-day week.
